packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-19 - unverified image-only reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure note: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading. The only identifying text seen is the modern pencilled shelfmark written on the fragments themselves (e.g. "Stams, STA, Frag. 15-1r" ... "15-8r"), which is part of the image.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- One photograph of eight separate fragments laid on black ground with colour checker (lower left) and cm scale (right edge). Each fragment carries a modern pencil label "Stams, STA, Frag. 15-Nr".
- Material looks like paper (laid/thin, translucent, stained), not parchment. All fragments carry music in mensural/modern-style notation on five-line staves (round/oval note heads with stems, bar lines in places), not liturgical chant neumes. Text underlay is sparse and in a cursive/humanistic hand.
- Fragments (positions as seen in overview):
  15-7r (upper left): heading "A 8. Secundo" (?) above a staff with clef, mensuration/time sign, notes; below the staff text "Lucis maccess: Vic..." (reading uncertain), and vertical text at right edge "Jo..." (?). Torn lower right.
  15-6r (top centre): long horizontal strip trimmed to a trapezoid; two staves of notes with bar lines; ink blots at right; decorative wavy line under lower staff.
  15-3r (upper right): small leaf with four short staff segments of notes at right side only; rest blank.
  15-8r (left, small slip): text only "...natus vam celi..." (?) under staff fragments.
  15-4r (centre): two joined pieces; large decorated initial "K" at left of upper piece; staves with notes; text underlay "Kyrie eleison" repeated ("ÿ" marks repeated text?); bottom line "...ibus bonae voluntatis laudamus te bene..." (reading tentative, see tile reading).
  15-5r (lower left of centre): ruled empty staves; a later inscription in the lower half "Am(?) ... IV/42 ... 1625" (?) - uncertain.
  15-2r (lower centre): large leaf, essentially blank, heavily stained/brushed surface; no visible notation in overview.
  15-1r (lower right): leaf with three staves of notes (dense, stemmed note heads), a line of text "... wir im Leben sind" (?) under first staff (German?), and a clef at the left of a fourth staff with ink damage.
- No running titles, no glosses. Interpretation (tentative): leaves/strips from part-books or choir parts of polyphonic music, some Mass (Kyrie/Gloria) text underlay.
- This overview is reduced; text is read below from tiles where available.

TILE image-002.jpg (native tile: fragment 15-7r, upper left of the group; top edge of 15-8r slip visible at bottom left)
Layout: vertical ruled margin line at left; a heading line; one staff (five lines) with clef, a sign looking like "C" with stroke (mensuration/time sign), a double bar/ligature-like block and a rest; notes with dots; a second staff segment begins at the right, lower, with bar lines (a separate part or a lower system). Below the first staff a text line; at the break, a word written vertically.
image-002 l.1 (heading): A 8. Secundo
   ("A" large flourished capital; "8." numeral; "Secundo" with long s. Tentative interpretation: "a 8" = for eight voices, "Secundo" = part/choir designation. Observation only.)
image-002 l.2 (staff): [clef] [time/mensuration sign] [rest/blocks] [dotted note] | | | [notes] - music, not transcribed.
image-002 l.3 (text under staff): Lucis maccess: Vi[...]
   ("Lucis" with large initial L; "maccess" - the word reads m-a-c-c-e-ss with a colon after; could be "mattess"? or an abbreviated form; "Vi" then a flourish/abbreviation, rest lost or obscured. Reading of word 2 uncertain: maccess?)
image-002 vertical text (written top-to-bottom, at right of l.3, beside the tear): Sponso (?)  - reads "Spons" + o/c?; uncertain, possibly a part label or text cue.
image-002 lower right torn flap: a few note heads on a staff segment, no text.
Unread/limits: right part of fragment torn away; second staff segment carries no legible text.

TILE image-003.jpg (overlaps image-002 at left: right end of 15-7r with "...cundo"; left end of strip 15-6r)
15-7r part: repeats heading "...cundo" and staff end already seen in image-002 (overlap, not new text); torn flap with two notes. No new text.
15-6r left end: two staves, each with a C-type clef at left; notes (breves/semibreves, rests), a bar line; a long ink-blot bar on lower staff; below lower staff a decorative wavy flourish line. Under the flourish, the tops of letters from a further line, cut by the trim ("l" ascenders only). No legible text.

TILE image-004.jpg (middle of strip 15-6r; overlaps image-003 at left; top of 15-2r leaf at bottom)
Two staves of notation with bar lines (four bar lines visible), semibreves/minims with dots, breves, rests; repeated wavy flourishes below the lower staff (one per bar). Bottom trim cuts through the tops of a further line: only ascenders and show-through visible; show-through of notation/text from the reverse is faintly visible between staves. No legible text on this tile.
Bottom of tile: top edge of leaf 15-2r, blank.

TILE image-005.jpg (right end of strip 15-6r, label "Stams, STA, Frg. 15-6r"; overlaps image-004; left edge of leaf 15-3r at right; top of 15-2r at bottom)
End of both staves: notes, ink corrosion holes/blots, final double bars with a flourished ending sign; at the right of each staff a spiral/"custos-like" flourish (end sign or signum). Final wavy flourish under lower staff. No text.
15-3r left margin (right of tile) and 15-2r top edge: blank.

TILE image-006.jpg (whole leaf 15-3r, label "Stams, STA, Frg. 15-3r")
Five short staff segments at the right of the leaf (top one cut at the top edge, showing only stems); each ends with a final double bar. Notation looks like later (more modern) notation: filled note heads with stems, flags/beams, a large slanted stroke (fermata-like or tie) before the final note; a clef-like "C" or bass-clef sign at the start of the second segment. Left half of leaf blank and stained. Leaf paste-over/folding line at right edge.
No text on this tile.

TILE image-007.jpg (slip 15-8r upper left; left part of 15-4r upper piece with initial; top of 15-5r lower right)
15-8r slip: bottom of a staff with stems/bar strokes at top (notes cut off); label "STA, Frg. 15 8r" (pencil, partly cut); one text line:
image-007 l.1 (15-8r): [.]atus vam cæli
   (first letter cut at left edge: a minim stroke, so "-natus" or "-uatus"/"-iatus" possible; "vam" could be "uam"; "cæli" with ae-ligature "æ", final i possibly with trailing stroke cut at edge. Read: "...atus vam cæli[...]")
15-4r upper piece (left portion): ruled left margin; a large outlined initial in cursive form, "K" (with looping stem and long tail) - read as K; to its right the clef of an upper staff (edge of tile); at bottom, bass-type clef "C/F" sign with dot(s) and a note on a lower staff.
15-5r top: label "Stams, ST[A...]", ruled empty staff lines. No text.

TILE image-008.jpg (15-4r: upper-left piece joined by a modern repair strip to the main piece; upper part of main piece; 15-5r at lower left)
Observation: the "ÿ" sign recurs alone under notes; it looks like the usual repetition sign (written "ij"/"ÿ") rather than a word. I transcribe it as ÿ.
Upper-left piece (left of the join):
image-008 l.1 (staff): [initial K in left margin, spanning staff + text] [clef] notes (minims/crotchets)
image-008 l.2 (text): ÿrieleison   (with the initial: K-ÿrieleison; "ÿ" for y with diaeresis; reads "[K]ÿrie(e)leison" with the two e's run together - written as one word "ÿrieleison" or "ÿrie eleison"; the e after "ri" ambiguous)
image-008 l.3 (staff): [bass-type clef] notes
Main piece (right of the join), physical lines from top of that piece:
image-008 r.1 (staff): notes (continuation of upper staff across the join)
image-008 r.2 (text): ÿ ... ÿ   (two repetition signs only; faint show-through between)
image-008 r.3 (staff): notes
image-008 r.4 (text): ÿ   Kÿrieelei[son]   ("Kÿrie" with capital K; continues off tile to right; see image-009)
image-008 r.5 (staff): notes, a rest
image-008 r.6 (text): son ,   ÿ   (end of "[elei]son" at left, a comma-like stroke, then ÿ)
image-008 r.7 (staff): [clef with mensuration/"3"? sign at very left, double bar] [second clef] notes - a new section begins here
image-008 r.8 (text): n .   Kÿrie e[...]   (stray "n" at left margin = end of preceding word; then large decorated initial K "Kÿrie e..." continuing right)
15-5r (lower left): empty staves, label "Stams, STA, Frg. 15-5r". No text.

TILE image-009.jpg (right half of 15-4r main piece, overlapping image-008; leaf 15-2r at right)
15-4r right half: vertical ruled line near right edge (staff end margin); at the right end of each staff a custos (direction mark) beyond the margin line; one staff has a final double bar with a clef-like sign (end of a section). Text lines (overlap with image-008 r.2-r.8):
image-009 l.1 (staff): notes [custos]
image-009 l.2 (text): ÿ   (one repetition sign; faint show-through)
image-009 l.3 (staff): notes, double bar + sign at right
image-009 l.4 (text): Kÿrieeleison   (this completes image-008 r.4: "Kÿrie eleison", written with the e's joined; final "-son" with long s)
image-009 l.5 (staff): notes [custos]
image-009 l.6 (text): ÿ   (right part of image-008 r.6)
image-009 l.7 (staff): notes [custos]
image-009 l.8 (text): Kÿrie eleÿ   (the large-initial line, = image-008 r.8; "eleÿ" - final ÿ either "elei-" with y-form or "eley[son]"; reads eley/eleÿ)
15-2r (right of tile): blank stained paper with brush-like marks (paste/adhesive residue?), small repairs at left edge; a faint pencil/grey vertical stroke near top. No text or notation visible.

TILE image-010.jpg (right half of 15-2r; bottom of 15-3r at top right; left edge of 15-1r at right)
15-2r: blank face, but faint show-through of notation from the reverse (note heads and stems in a row across the middle, very faint) - no legible text. Brushed adhesive marks.
15-1r left edge: staff with note heads (rhomboid/lozenge-headed minims with stems); text line under first staff, left part:
image-010 l.1 (15-1r, text): [.] wir im Lebe[n]   (first letter cut/faint; "wir im Leben" - German; overlaps the overview reading "...wir im Leben sind")
Rest of 15-1r on next tile.

TILE image-011.jpg (bottom of 15-3r with label "Stams, STA, Frg. 15-3r"; upper part of 15-1r, overlaps image-010)
15-3r bottom: blank.
15-1r: a vertical line/fold divides the leaf (possibly the join of two pasted pieces or a fold); staff lines are faint (ruled lightly, only some lines visible); notes are large lozenge/rhomboid heads with stems, written over the faint staves; breves (square with side strokes) in the second row.
image-011 l.1 (staff 1): notes across both halves
image-011 l.2 (text, left half only): [.]wir im Leben sind   followed by a large sign like "S" or "§" (above the next staff; possibly a signum/repeat mark)
   (first letter of the line at the left edge partially visible; "wir" first letter w with looped form; "Leben" with initial L; "sind" with long s.)
image-011 l.3 (staff 2): notes across both halves, two breves in right half
image-011 l.4 (staff 3, bottom edge): stems only; ink blot/damage at left.
No further text on this tile.

TILE image-012.jpg (colour checker at left; lower part of 15-5r at right)
15-5r: ruled empty staves (five-line, ink); no notes. Over the staves a modern pencil note (not the music scribe), two lines:
